**Finding: Compliant** (rule LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer)

I reviewed the financial provisions (Art. IX), termination and effects-of-termination provisions (Art. XII), and the liability/indemnification article (Art. XIV), plus full-text searches for "liquidated damages" and "penalty" (no hits).

Key points:
- **No Customer-payable LD or penalty exists.** Sanofi's payment obligations are limited to the $50M upfront, capped milestones ($520M aggregate), royalties on Net Sales, and the U.S. profit/loss share — all performance-linked, not penal.
- **Late-payment interest only** (§ 9.6): reciprocal, LIBOR + [***]%, capped at the maximum lawful rate. The rule's detection guidance expressly treats ordinary late-payment interest as not a deviation.
- **No early-termination fee.** § 12.2(a)(i) lets Sanofi terminate for convenience on notice alone, with no minimum fee or termination payment. The post-termination royalties in § 12.3(c)(ii)C run *from RevMed to Sanofi*, which benefits our party.
- **Diligence failure (§ 5.7)** is not backed by a fixed sum; § 12.6 carves § 5.7 out of the "termination is not the sole remedy" rule, i.e. termination is the remedy there.

This sits at the **preferred** position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer), so no redline was proposed.
